name: Automation Runtime Reconciliation & State Efficiency
changes: Prunes old Automation runtime targets whose canonical item IDs no longer exist in a valid authoritative media-library.json, with a 24-hour grace window and fail-safe parsing.
Gives library-proven imported/satisfied target states semantic precedence over stale searching/queueing/queued/grabbed/waiting writes while allowing a real newer grab action to proceed.
Adds Automation runtime efficiency telemetry for target/orphan counts, runtime bytes, prune counts, reclaimed bytes and stale-state demotions blocked.
Normalizes unmistakable legacy v3.6.56 duplicate-content hold history to failure_class=import_integrity_hold without reconstructing or reactivating current target policy state.
Measures server-side diagnostics report construction time explicitly before considering formatted-report caching.
Preserves v3.6.57 Integrity Hold/count semantics, v3.6.55 no-op terminal-history efficiency, private SABnzbd 5.1.2 authority and the established Windows runtime handoff.
regression_guards: Old parseable orphan targets are pruned only when media-library.json parses successfully; recent or unparseable target records remain fail-safe.
A stale later scheduler write cannot demote a library-proven imported TV episode back to grabbed/queued/searching/waiting.
A genuinely newer grab with last_grab_ts after the final imported/satisfied timestamp is not suppressed.
Legacy byte-identical Smart Import held-for-review terminal evidence normalizes historically without creating active Automation holds.
Diagnostics expose automation runtime efficiency, stale-state reconciliation counters and diagnostics_report_build_ms timing.
All v3.6.57/v3.6.56/v3.6.55 guards remain mandatory and SAB transfer/repair/extraction behavior is unchanged.
